text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a major report released yesterday by the Productivity Commission, the Federal Government was urged to overhaul the A$4.5 billion private health insurance industry to help salvage the health system. The report suggested Medicare would also need to be studied if the Government wished to fully solve the problems of the health insurance industry. Page 1.

A spokesman for Finance Minister John Fahey said last night the Office of Asset Sales is likely to undertake a six week study for the Federal Government into the sale potential of Australian National and National Rail Corp. The study will examine both freight and passenger rail operators, with expressions of interest sought in Australian National by the end of January. Page 2.

Despite a refusal by New South Wales to change its industrial relations laws to be in line with the Federal system, Federal Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith said yesterday all States had responded well to the Federal Government's push for legislative changes to underpin its Workplace Relations Act. Page 5.

The Australian Tax Office has ruled to lock in its decision which makes previously exempt employer child-care schemes subject to fringe benefits tax (FBT). The ruling, when first drafted earlier this year, was attacked by accounting firms, child-care centres and the New South Wales Chamber of Commerce. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Productivity Commission has released a report recommending the health insurance system be changed to allow health funds to introduce no-claim bonuses that reward loyalty but also penalise older people taking out insurance cover. The report also critiises the Federal Government's tax rebate for failing to cut health costs, yet has been endorsed by Federal Health Minister Michael Wooldridge. Page 1.

News Corporation Ltd chairman Rupert Murdoch said yesterday the Federal Government must embark upon a far more radical reform agenda to ensure Australia does not become a backwater. Murdoch believes Australia's industrial relations system must be ovehauled and called for the country's tax system to be freed up. Page 1.

AGB McNair's NetWatch survey has found the number of Australians who have used the Internet has almost doubled from 1.4 million to 2.6 million over the past 15 months. The survey, of 4000 people aged over 14, suggested the most frequent users are cinema-goers, travellers, and vehicle buyers, and provided evidence that the Internet can be used as a feasible consumer marketing channel. Page 3.

Tasmanian surgeon Michael Wertheimer said yesterday the Federal Government's expensive breast cancer detection programme should be scrapped, as it is bureaucratic, and could lead to unnecessary operations. However, the National Breast Cancer Centre has called for national guidelines for doctors to detect the disease. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

United States-based media mogul Rupert Murdoch has used an ABC television interview in Japan to criticise the Federal Government, warning Australia was at risk of becoming a backwater if more rigorous economic reforms were not pursued. Senior ministers have reacted angrily, claiming Murdoch is waging a calculated campaign against the government. Page 1.

Sweeping changes recommended to the Federal Government in a Productivity Commission draft report on private health insurance would see the elderly and sick having to wait longer on health insurance claims, and young and healthy people being rewarded for taking up private health cover. Page 1.

Sydney's arts community has welcomed an agreement between the Sydney City Council and AMP Investments that will see the City gain a 1,200 seat rent-free recital hall as part of a A$300 million office tower development on AMP's difficult L-shaped Angel Place site. Page 1.

Powerful conglomerates from Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia have welcomed Brierley Investment's 20 percent acquisition of John Fairfax Holdings, knowing the sale will give them a foot in the door in three of Australia's major newspapers. Brierley is 2 per cent-owned by Malex Industries of Malaysia, which includes the Salim group of Simo-Indonesian billionaire Liem Sioe Liong, and 5.6 per cent owned by Temasek Holdings (Pte.) Ltd of Singapore. Page 1.
THE AGE

A study commissioned by Racing Victoria has found the Victorian racing industry generated a record A$174 million in economic activity as a result of the 1996 spring racing carnival. The figure is up 20 per cent from last year and can be attributed to a flamboyant marketing campaign, good weather on major race days, and a protracted wrangle over race broadcasts between Sky Channel and Tabcorp. Page A1.

The killing of six Red Cross workers in Chechnya marred the homecoming of Australian nurse and Red Cross worker Maree Worthington, who returned home after surviving on goat's liver and putrid water for 39 days in Sudan, where she was held hostage by Sudanese rebels. Worthington said she was "very disturbed" by the tragedy, yet says she had no regrets about working for the Red Cross. Page A1.

Australian Red Cross secretary-general Jim Charlton said yesterday the Australian Red Cross will continue to send workers into war zones, despite increasing security fears. Charlton said that despite concerns, humanitarianism had to continue on the battlefield. Page A1.

Victorian Treasurer Alan Stockdale has played down any hope of tax cuts for the State, despite the recording of a surplus of A$2.1 billion for the first quarter of 1996-97. Current account figures up to A$737.1 million from A$363 million last year are the one-off proceeds from privatisation, he said. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
